config.title: forwardRef & Exposing DOM Nodes

intro.title: forwardRef & Exposing DOM Nodes
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a custom form input component that can be directly focused from a parent component. You'll learn how to use React's forwardRef function to pass a ref through a component to access its underlying DOM node. This involves TypeScript for type safety and React hooks like useRef to create and manage refs. By the end, you'll understand how to expose DOM nodes from custom components for imperative actions like focusing or measuring elements.
intro.usecase: In real-world applications, forwardRef is essential for creating reusable, accessible UI components that need direct DOM manipulation. For example, in complex dashboards with multiple interactive charts, you might use forwardRef to expose the underlying canvas element of a custom Chart component, allowing parent components to programmatically trigger exports or capture screenshots. Similarly, in form libraries or design systems, forwardRef enables wrapping native input elements in custom styled Input or Textarea components while still allowing parent forms to focus, select text, or integrate with validation libraries that require direct DOM access. This pattern is also critical for building accessible modal dialogs, where a parent component needs to programmatically return focus to a triggering button after the modal closes.

objectives: Implement forwardRef to pass a ref from a parent component to a child component
Configure a custom component to expose its internal DOM node via forwardRef
Initialize and manipulate refs to access DOM elements in TypeScript
Apply TypeScript generics with forwardRef to type refs for specific DOM elements
Construct a form component that exposes its input element for direct focus control
Integrate forwardRef patterns with event handlers to control child component behavior
Update component props to accept and forward refs while maintaining type safety
